terms.grammar: adjective, with mēnsis; also a masculine noun (sc. mēnsis)
terms.comment: Named after Augustus, who gave his name to Sextīlis rather than to September, the month of his birth, because his first consulship and his great victories fell in it (Suet. Aug. 31.2). Kalendae, Nōnae, Īdūs Augustae: the 1st, 5th and 13th.

terms.grammar: adjective, with mēnsis; also a masculine noun (sc. mēnsis)
terms.comment: The sixth month, counting from March (sextus).

phrases.english: poets giving readings in August (one of the horrors of Rome)

phrases.latin: quīnque diēs tibi pollicitus mē rūre futūrum, Sextīlem tōtum mendāx dēsīderor
phrases.english: I promised you I would be in the country five days, and I am missed the whole of August, a liar

sources: Lewis & Short: Augustus · Lewis & Short: Sextilis
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 77–78.
